sections.h2: Selling in a young, fast-growing Melissa
sections.html:
Melissa is small, young and almost entirely owner-occupied, so most competing listings are recent construction. An older or unrenovated house has to stand next to builder product with current finishes.

Melissa counted 4,695 residents in 2010 and 13,901 in 2020. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 29,969, which is 115.6 percent more than 2020 and ranks among the quickest gains in Texas. Children are 30.7 percent of the population, while just 6.7 percent of people are 65 or older.

  • Listing with an agent works for a tidy house when you can spare several weeks.
  • Selling on your own fits an owner at ease with contracts and disclosures.
  • A cash offer fits a house needing repairs, one with a tenant, or a sale against the clock.

Homeowners dominate here, and incomes are high. Between 2020 and 2024, 88.7 percent of homes were lived in by their owners, the median value reached $454,000 and the median household income was $138,763.

The mean commute is 33.6 minutes, so plenty of residents work elsewhere in the Dallas area. Larger households of about three people mean buyers often start by asking about bedrooms and yard space.

You will find Melissa along U.S. Highway 75, roughly seven miles northeast of McKinney, in the north central part of Collin County. A railroad brought the 1872 townsite, and growth stayed slow for about a century.

Incorporation came in the early 1970s, with 604 residents in 1980 and 1,350 in 2000. Nearly everything people buy and sell in Melissa was built after that, so the typical house on the market is quite new.

sections.h2: Collin County offices for Melissa sellers
sections.html:
Collin County offices handle Melissa houses. Exemption filings and value questions belong to the Collin Central Appraisal District. The county clerk is the one who files your deed.

  • Look up your account on the district's property search and make sure your homestead exemption shows up.
  • A protest of value goes to the Collin appraisal review board.
  • New subdivisions may carry special district charges, so ask what appears on your bill.

Ask the county tax office for the amount due before the closing date.

A casita, garage apartment or similar extra building on your lot calls for a look at Melissa's rules on second dwellings. The city has allowed accessory dwelling units only in its larger single-family zones, on lots over 10,000 square feet, with review of parking, spacing and setbacks. State law can change what a city allows, so ask the planning staff what applies to your lot today.

  • Confirm with the city that every added structure on the lot was permitted.
  • Round up permits and final inspections for any addition. Lenders and inspectors both request them.
  • Check your HOA documents, because most newer Melissa subdivisions have them.

Unpermitted work often pushes back a closing date. Settling it before you list leaves the schedule under your control.

sections.h2: How Texas property tax dates affect a newer Melissa home
sections.html:
January 1 is when a year's tax lien attaches and when the appraisal district fixes your house's value. A sale in, say, June means the buyer inherits a bill that has been building for months.

  • Homeowners get $140,000 off the value used for school taxes, and those who are 65 or older or disabled get another $60,000 on top.
  • If you never claimed it, the person who buys from you after January 1 may still apply for the rest of that year.
  • Homestead valuation notices arrive about April 1, and exemption filings must come in before May 1.

At Melissa values the tax split is a sizable closing line, so have the title company walk you through it before signing.

sections.h2: Selling with a tenant, an heir or a default
sections.html:
Rentals are uncommon at a median rent of $2,532, and the typical buyer plans to move in. If a tenant lives there, expect to serve a three day written notice to vacate unless the lease sets something else. A tenant who refuses to leave ends up in justice court. Work your closing date backward from the lease end.

Inherited house? A will can be offered for probate within four years of the death, or heirs can file a muniment of title or affidavit of heirship with the county clerk. Behind on the loan? A notice of sale reaches you at least 21 days before the auction, and that window is when a sale can still save your equity.

Families with kids dominate the buyer pool: 7.1 percent of residents are under five and 30.7 percent are under 18. They commute, so access to U.S. Highway 75 and travel time to McKinney and Dallas come up often. Most shopping happens close by.

  • Show recent upgrades, because competing listings are nearly new.
  • Gather HOA documents and any warranty paperwork early.
  • Be ready for a buyer whose own house must sell first, which can lengthen a closing.

Nearly a quarter of residents speak another language at home (23.9 percent), so being flexible about how you communicate with buyers helps.

sections.h2: Why Melissa has so many buyers
sections.html:
A lot of people have moved into a small area. Land grew from 10.11 square miles in 2010 to 11.45, yet density jumped from 464.3 to 1,213.8 people per square mile by 2020.

Just 81.6 percent of residents had the same address a year before, a sign of steady newcomers. Sellers get lively buyer traffic from that, though it also means neighbors on your street may have arrived recently. Newer subdivisions bring uniform lots, so condition, upgrades and the location of your lot within the neighborhood tend to set the price spread.

In practice that means a tidy yard, fresh paint and a clear story about what you have improved since you bought. Buyers walking through several near-identical homes in a day remember the one that felt finished, and they will pay attention to any open permit or unfinished project.

Pull your deed, latest tax statement, HOA papers and mortgage payoff letter together before offers arrive. After you say yes, a title company hunts for liens, unpaid taxes and breaks in the ownership chain. Each item it turns up needs clearing before the deed gets signed and recorded by the county clerk. A cash purchase usually skips the inspection and lender appraisal that a retail sale adds, so the calendar can run shorter. If the buyer's money comes from selling another house, ask early whether that sale is firm, since a chain of contracts can stretch a closing.

faqs.q: Which county is Melissa, TX in?
faqs.a: Collin County, in its north central part near McKinney. The Collin Central Appraisal District and county clerk handle your values and deed.
Very fast. The city had 13,901 residents in 2020 and an estimated 29,969 on July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Melissa house with a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes, though many buyers want to move in. Check the lease end date and give written notice if you need the tenant out.

faqs.q: What exemption applies to a Melissa homestead?
faqs.a: The base is $140,000 from the school district, with $60,000 added at age 65 or on disability. Apply to the appraisal district by the end of April.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell my late parent's Melissa house?
faqs.a: Usually some court or recorded step comes first. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death skips probate.
